tasks.title: Component-literal scanner as a Rust test whose needles come from the LIVE registry, with a counted allowlist
tasks.gate: §19.3 production literal scanner planted-positive; three mandatory reverse cases (a) discovery-derived needle (b) namespaced FQN (c) un-allowlisted new module

plantedFailure.edit: plant the namespaced FQN `lingxi-local-app:local-app-build` (NOT the basename) into apps/engine-mobile/src/local_apps_host.rs

tasks.notes:
§19.3's literal wording — `tasks/src` and `tools/workflow/src` contain no Local App workflow basename — CANNOT be green on landing, because Phase -1 step 1 explicitly KEEPS both existing registrations (tools/workflow/src/builtins.rs plus three .js files in that directory). Ship the allowlist explicit and counted, reaching 0 only at Phase 9. Without the count, the obvious way to make the red gate green is to exempt the directory, which silently disables the scanner for all of tools/workflow/. The count is the thing that makes that visible.

SCOPED AT lap/baseline. §19.3's reverse case (a) as written needs a verified Plugin inventory, which does not exist until Phase 0a/2. §18 step 7 is explicit that Phase -1 derives needles from the EXISTING live registries and Phase 2 switches to Plugin inventory. At Phase -1 the live source is mobile_skill_registry() (apps/engine-mobile/src/lib.rs:383 -> skill_api::register_mobile), so case (a) becomes: add a skill to the live registry, confirm the needle set GROWS, then plant that new name in local_apps_host.rs and require red. That is why this is a Rust test and not a python grep gate — a python scanner cannot call into the registry, and a needle list it kept itself would be the static array the gate exists to forbid.

KNOWN COUPLING, adjudicated after the write stage. The scanner's WORKFLOW needles are derived from `tool_workflow::LOCAL_APP_BUILD_WORKFLOWS` (tools/workflow/src/lib.rs:310) — which is the array P-1.9 DELETES. This is an ordering defect in the decomposition, not in the writer's judgment: P-1.0 was sequenced first and pointed at P-1.9's deletion target. The alternative live source, `BUILTIN_WORKFLOWS` (tools/workflow/src/builtins.rs:93), does survive Phase -1 — Phase -1 step 1 keeps both registrations — but it also contains `deep-research`, and no property distinguishing a Local App workflow from it exists until P-1.6 introduces LocalAppWorkflowTaskScope. So the bootstrap is real. Resolution: keep this source, and make P-1.9 responsible for re-pointing the scanner. When P-1.9 deletes the array this test FAILS TO COMPILE, which is loud and correct. The only wrong resolution is hardcoding the two names here — that turns the gate into the static array it exists to forbid.

tasks.notes:
DESCRIPTOR CORRECTED after the verify pass ran lap_gate.py against it and it FAILED. Two errors, both mine, both from writing the descriptor out of the design's §19.3 wording without checking the symbols exist in this codebase:
  - plantedFailure named `host_context`, which does not exist anywhere in the local-apps surface. The     only workspace hits are the unrelated permission classifier (permission/src/host_context.rs). A gate     whose must-name string cannot appear can never pass.
  - owns named local_apps_host.rs + local_app_plugin_binding.rs; the uncovered half of §19.3 is actually     the workflow-args seam in workflow_support.rs. The profile/surface half in local_apps_host.rs already     HAS tests at HEAD (create_rejects_runtime_profile_and_surface_overrides,     scaffold_rejects_an_empty_brief_and_an_unknown_surface, create_app_in_shell_mode_rejects_a_surface),     so testing there would have been redundant while the workflow injection had nothing.

The lesson generalises: a descriptor written from design prose can name a symbol the code does not have, and `lap-gate.sh tasks` cannot catch that — it validates that a must-name string EXISTS, not that it is REACHABLE. Descriptors for later phases should be re-grounded against the code before their task starts.

tasks.notes:
The map is at workflow_support.rs:1286-1290 at lap/baseline. Anchor on the symbol, never the line.

THREE OBSERVATIONS FROM P-1.1'S VERIFICATION — for this task, not defects in P-1.1.
1. ALL_BUILD_TARGETS is a hardcoded [LocalAppBuildTarget; 5]. A new variant DOES hard-error in expected_binding's wildcard-free match (proven: adding a 6th gave error[E0004] at both local_app_plugin_binding.rs:119 and workflow_support.rs:1192), but filling in that arm alone compiles and passes — nothing ties the array length to the variant count, so the new mapping would ship unexercised. If this task reshapes the routing, tie iteration to the enum.
2. The `is pinned to runtime profile {family}, which` clause is asserted by nothing. All four refusal assertions check the app id plus the ordered `must use ...; refusing caller-selected workflow ...` fragment, so dropping the family from the message leaves the suite green. Diagnostic quality, not security content — but the binding's doc claims the family is preserved and that claim is unpinned.
3. `{app_id:?}` vs `{app_id}` is unpinned; contains("demo1234") passes either way, so the debug quoting could silently become plain. Cosmetic.

tasks.title: Cut the workflow-name trigger binding in skill-api, and pin the two look-alikes that must NOT be touched
tasks.gate: §19.3 no Local App component name carries authority outside the composition binding

plantedFailure.edit: restore "local-app-build" to the create-local-app skill's triggers array in bundled.rs

tasks.notes:
FOUND BY THE P-1.0 VERIFICATION PASS, outside the three scan roots, and confirmed by hand at lap/baseline.

THE DEFECT. skill-api/src/builtin/bundled.rs:43 gives the create-local-app SKILL the trigger array ["create local app", "local app", "local-app-build"]. The third entry is a WORKFLOW name used as a skill trigger phrase — a cross-component name binding, which is exactly the shape §19.3 exists to remove. It is genuine production code: there is no #[cfg(test)] above that line. Phase 4 merges the two workflows, at which point this trigger silently stops matching and nothing in the suite notices. The skill NAMES in the same file are the definition site and are legitimately unscannable; the trigger is not.

⛔ THE LOOK-ALIKE THAT MUST NOT BE 'FIXED'. traits/src/mobile_linux.rs:46 declares LOCAL_APP_BUILD_ROOT = "/var/lingxi/local-app-build". That string coincides with a workflow name but is a FILESYSTEM MOUNT ROOT, not a reference to the workflow. It carries no name-derived authority, and renaming it to track a renamed workflow would silently move a path on real devices — the same class of silent data loss as renaming a SQLite table, which nothing in this repo would catch. Add it to the allowlist with this reasoning if traits/src ever enters the scan surface; do not touch the value.

TEMPLATES, for the record. local-apps/templates/runtime-profiles/** is compiled into production wholesale by include_bytes! via the profile_file! macro, and the scanner cannot see it. Grepped at lap/baseline: it contains ZERO component-name needles today. That is a fact with a date on it, not a guarantee — it is the tree runtime-profile work touches, so the Phase 1 packer (P1.2) should carry the assertion rather than this scanner.

SCOPE. Deliberately NOT solved by widening SCAN_ROOTS. Adding skill-api/src and traits/src would make the scanner red on landing for two occurrences of very different kinds, and the cheapest way to green that is an allowlist entry — which would preserve the defect while looking like it had been handled.
